ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly high-intensity (white/light-grey) central field (~85%) contrasted against low-intensity (black/dark-grey) perimeter borders and focal mottle points (~15%).
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Large contiguous light-grey field covering the central lobes. Distinct low-intensity black banding (approx. 5-15 pixel width) follows the entire trailing edge contour. Small, isolated low-intensity pixel clusters are distributed across the medial region of the left lobe.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Acute V-shaped notch with a calculated internal angle of approximately 65 degrees and a vertical pixel depth equivalent to 8% of the total fluke height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serrations with pixel amplitudes ranging from 3 to 12 pixels. The left lobe exhibits more rounded, frequent peaks, while the right lobe contains sharper, sawtooth-like indentations including a large terminal notch at the tip.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Bi-lobed convex curve originating from the median notch, transitioning to a slight concavity before reaching the elevated, upward-sweeping tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Spatial cluster of approx. 5-7 low-intensity focal spots in the lower-medial quadrant of the left lobe; additional sparse spotting visible near the midline of the right lobe.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: A single, distinct low-intensity linear disruption (~40 pixels in length) oriented at 110 degrees on the left lobe, cutting through the white pigmentation field.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: A significant irregular indentation and upward-hooked projection on the distal tip of the right lobe lobe, distinct from standard serration patterns.
other_distinctive_markers: A series of vertical drip-like pigmentation artifacts originating from the dark trailing edge border into the light central field on the left lobe.
